A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Shuffle-R1 with the same core framework and retained experiments. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: V3 reports original RL training results, benchmark evaluations, component ablations, efficiency analyses and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds algorithm comparisons, an ABS-only control, wall-clock analyses, and experiments on larger models and additional tasks.

M1.justification: The max–min pairing, pair retention, weighted resampling and Algorithm 1 are retained. V4 introduces an IoU-based soft-reward adaptation for referring-expression comprehension and corrects the stated clipped objective by placing the advantage inside both branches of the minimum in Eq. 1. The equation correction does not establish that the original experiments' implementation changed.

E1.justification: V4 retains the visual-reasoning coverage and adds referring-expression comprehension on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg. It also adds language-only training on Open-S1 and evaluation on Math12K, AIME24, MATH500, GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond and OlympiadBench (Section 4.4), substantially broadening task and input coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds GSPO to the Geometry3K and K12 comparisons in Tables 1–2. For the existing 30k-data, 7B setting, new Table 10 adds direct GRPO, DAPO and GSPO comparisons beyond v3's comparison with separately developed models. The earlier model comparators, RLOO, REINFORCE++ and prioritized replay remain.

E3.justification: Added experimental protocols include Qwen2.5-VL-32B trained for 50 steps on 30k samples, a 3B REC experiment using 60k samples, and Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B trained for 150 steps. V4 also introduces a random-pair control isolating ABS. The previously documented Geometry3K/K12 budgets and core hyperparameter settings are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds ABS without PTS to isolate its contribution (Table 4), accuracy-versus-GPU-hour curves across update sizes (Figure 7), and benchmark-level sensitivity results for sampling ratio and shuffle count (Table 12). These materially extend the component and efficiency analyses. Earlier hyperparameter curves, replay comparisons and four case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean pass@1 over eight independent evaluation runs at temperature 0.5. V4 introduces no new training-seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The matched headline results remain unchanged, including Shuffle-R1-7B's 64.7 average in Table 3. V4 adds substantial results: Table 10 reports averages of 62.5 for GRPO, 63.4 for DAPO and 62.8 for GSPO against the retained 64.7; Table 6 reports 69.1 versus GRPO's 67.4 at 32B. REC, text-only, ABS-only, sensitivity and GPU-hour results are also newly reported, rather than improvements to the retained models between versions.

T1.justification: New Appendix H introduces a Gaussian advantage assumption, a threshold-selection approximation, and three propositions with derivations concerning advantage magnitude, gradient norms and sampling bias. V3 has no corresponding theoretical analysis. V4 also corrects the clipped objective and changes the written ABS normalization to the global batch B, consistent with the retained pseudocode.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: diagnosing Advantage Collapsing and Rollout Silencing, addressing them with PTS and ABS, improving multimodal generalization, and matching GRPO with roughly half the training steps. The added experiments principally expand support for these claims.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the ABS-only experiment as evidence of independent component utility and extends applicability discussion to soft-reward and text-only tasks. Appendix H adds a directional positive-bias explanation absent from v3. Existing explanations involving over-pruning, diminishing resampling returns, stale replay samples and qualitative reasoning improvements are largely retained.

D1.justification: V4 identifies the previously unspecified 80GB GPUs as NVIDIA H800-80G-SXM, supplies absolute GPU-hour measurements, and documents model identities, sample counts and budgets for the extension experiments. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed hardware for retained experiments. Existing prompts, hyperparameter tables, pseudocode and project/code references remain.

R1.justification: V4 adds GSPO and references supporting the new text-only models, training data and benchmarks. It removes citations to Allen-Zhu and Li (2024), Ye et al. (2024), Du et al. (2024) and Yue et al. (2024). The main positioning around dynamic data selection and resampling remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: V4 substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction, preliminaries and several analysis/results passages. It incorporates Preliminaries into Method, moves supplementary experimental results ahead of settings and dataset appendices, and adds separate acknowledgment, ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. This constitutes broad narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to the single-column ICLR format, with extensive figure/table relocation, captions above tables and highlighted result rows. V4 adds a pipeline-comparison schematic, wall-clock panels and several tables, replaces relative timing annotations with GPU-hour labels, and compresses the four retained case-study figures onto one page.

improvement.justification: The matched 30k algorithm comparison, ABS-only control and GPU-time curves strengthen evidence for the central empirical efficiency claim; REC and text-only experiments broaden its support. The net gain is limited by an error in the new theoretical appendix: Proposition 3 claims positive mean advantage, but its symmetric Gaussian model with absolute-value weighting preserves zero signed mean. Thus the empirical case improves while the added theoretical justification is partly unsound.
